Nyberg (MP II 192) was on the right track in looking for a Sanskritic name, though his proposal seems off the mark. Rather than look for a proper name perhaps the place to start is with a title. While a *tātraº makes little sense, a pātraº would. Among the meanings is a well-attested 'king's counselor, minister.' Occasionally in Phl Mss scribes confuse t and p , especially when the former is part of a ligature. I have no solid suggestion for YfnTEº, unless, partially with Nyberg, it stands for ºgatas 'having gone.' He might have announced himself at court with pātrâgato'smi 'I have come as minister' and this was taken as his title. This would make sense of the inexplicable zīwā wuzurgmihr YfnTER__TXt ī amāh (§8). That is, Xursraw, knowing that the Persians have won, ironically refers to his vizier with the Indian title. Later in §18 we have only wuzurgmihr ī amāh. See Daryaee Iranian Studies 35, 2002, 286.
